newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: POLISH FLOODS DELAY S.AFRICA UNICORN TANKER LAUNCH.
newsitem.headline: POLISH FLOODS DELAY S.AFRICA UNICORN TANKER LAUNCH.

text.p: The launch of a 45,000 deadweight tonne tanker built in Poland for South Africa's Unicorn Tankers, has been delayed by heavy flooding in Poland, marine director Robert Young said on Wednesday.

The ship, named Hambisa and valued at $36 million will be used by Shell South Africa and BP Southern Africa to fulfill their southern African and Indian Ocean transport requirements, Young told reporters.

The tanker was built at Poland's Szczecin shipyard and is the fourth 45,000 dwtchemical products tanker to be built at the shipyard for Unicorn, a division of Unicorn Lines (Pty) Ltd which is part of the Grindrod Unicorn Group Ltd . The tanker was due to be launched on July 26.
It was built to a high specification developed by Unicorn and approved by Shell International and incorporates advanced technology and equipment.

It will join three other Polish-built tankers, two of which were launched late last year and are used by Engen Ltd. The third vessel was launched last month was built and designed for Shell Australia's coastal product trade.

"Our investment in the four Polish (new ships) and a 14,000dwt chemical tanker makes evident our commitment to pursuing this specialised market," Unicorn Tankers chief executive Alan Olivier said in a statement.
